text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Boris Yeltsin's and Bill Clinton's Helsinki summit to be held at President's residence, Mantyniemi.
- Structural economic change has led Finnish insurance sector to situation where the bold and fast benefit at the expense of the gullible, says Asmo Kalpala, CEO of mutual insurer Tapiola.
- Almost 100 little schools in rural Finland may be closed this year due to spending cuts. @
- UN human rights envoy to former Yugoslavia Elisabeth Rehn says she will be available to become UN's human rights commissioner if asked.
- Estonian army taking after Finnish army model.
- Finland and Latvia start bilateral talks on abandoning visa requirements.
- Three of four children in a Helsinki elementary shool (ages 6-13) know what alcohol tastes like and one of four have already tasted tobacco, survey shows. @

- Helsinki telephone company HPY's operating result doubled to 140 million markka last year and the profit before extraordinary items almost tripled, helped by mobile phone operator Radiolinja of which HPY owns 47 percent.
- Finland's telecommunications authority to ban sales of analogue NMT mobile phones which do not have a security code and can be altered for calls at others' expense.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Some stocks' dividend yields are higher than long bond yields despite clear stock market gains in a year -- a sign of undervaluation, asset manager says. @
- National carrier Finnair is losing millions of markka due to wildcat strikes in a prolonged conflict between air control officers and the airport authority.

- State-owned Postipankki to arrange the listing and offering of Helsinki telephone operator Helsingin Puhelin Oy due in the autumn, the says Kurt Nordman, managing director of the company's owner HPY.
AAMULEHTI
- European Commisssion says it will help Finland find a solution to a cargo truck dispute between Finland and Russia. @
- Improper storage of unpasteurised milk has caused salmonella in Ostrobotnia in western Finland.
DEMARI
- The Green Party celebrates 10th anniversary this week.

- President Urho Kekkonen's decision to open Finland's foreign trade in 1957 and later to join the European Free Trade Association EFTA established its integration with the west, says a new dissertitation.
